records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Feed HTML is saved with raw_html cooking without sanitization, so scripts or event handlers supplied by a feed author execute in the forum origin.
records.rationale: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html; Post#cook returns `raw` unfiltered (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), and best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. No sanitization step exists anywhere in the diff for feed/imported HTML, so script tags or event handlers from a feed/article are executed in the forum's origin.

records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — Failed retrievals have no terminal state, so this unconditional reload repeatedly enqueues work and leaves embeds loading until the source recovers.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: embed/loading.html.erb contains an unconditional setTimeout reload every 30s with no failure state, and embed_controller.rb enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic every time no TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed matches, so failed retrievals (e.g., feed fetch fails or content never imports) cause an unbounded reload/retry loop with no terminal message. Note the impact is partially mitigated by TopicRetriever's 60s Redis throttle and host check, and the retry loop is arguably intentional for transient failures — so this is a design/robustness concern a maintainer would

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Each cache-miss retrieval runs the entire feed poll before checking the requested URL, so concurrent new embeds multiply full-feed parsing and per-item import work and can saturate job workers.
records.rationale: Verified in the diff: perform_retrieve in lib/topic_retriever.rb calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` on every cache-miss retrieval before falling back to fetch_http, and PollFeed parses the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and imports every item. Since EmbedController#best enqueues RetrieveTopic for any unknown embed_url, concurrent first-time embeds each re-run the full feed poll and per-item import inside the worker, a concrete performance/worker-saturation concern created by this design (not an outright correctness defect).

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — TopicRetriever synchronously invokes the scheduled PollFeed job, coupling single-page retrieval to full-feed import policy and making future job lifecycle changes affect embeds.
records.rationale: The diff shows `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` in TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, confirming the finding: an on-demand single-URL retrieval synchronously executes the entire scheduled feed-polling job inline. This is a real, specific design/architecture coupling — full-feed fetching (potentially long-running network I/O) is invoked within a per-request retrieval job and the return path depends on whether the whole feed happens to contain the embed_url. It is not a correctness defect verifiable from the diff, but it is a concrete, decision-relevant maintainability/performance concern grounded
records.stripped_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — TopicRetriever synchronously invokes the scheduled PollFeed job, coupling single-page retrieval to full-feed import policy and making future job lifecycle changes affect embeds.
